chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jumhoor narrated from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jumhoor from his father from Sulayman ibn Sama'a from Abul Jarood who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far: If the Imam al-Qa'im from the Ahl al-Bayt passes away, with what will the one who comes after him be recognized? He said: With guidance and calmness/gravity, and the acknowledgment of the family of Muhammad of his virtue, and he will not be asked about anything in the east or the west unless he answers.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House, referring to the Prophet's family
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Rising One, a title for the twelfth Imam
key_terms.بَيْنَ صَدْفَيْهِ: Between the two sides (east and west), implying comprehensiveness

ai.seo_question: What are the signs to recognize the next Imam after the death of Imam al-Qa'im?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani highlights the criteria for recognizing the successor of Imam al-Qa'im, emphasizing 'al-huda' (divine guidance) and 'al-ithraq' (a demeanor of calmness and gravity) as key indicators. It underscores the consensus of the Ahl al-Bayt in affirming his superiority and his infallible-like knowledge, capable of answering any question posed to him. This reflects the Shia belief in the continuity of spiritual authority and the distinct characteristics of the Imamate.
